name: build-toolchain-pins
body: Build toolchains are pinned so a release is reproducible, exactly where the toolchain mechanism or the closest build path can enforce it. Rust is exact on every path: a root `rust-toolchain.toml` (`channel = 1.98.1`) is found by rustup's parent-walk from the apg crate and all three cargo frontend crates, and CI uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.98.1`. Node is build-enforced: `src/tslib/.npmrc` sets `engine-strict=true`, and CI uses `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: '26.9.0'`. Go is exact on the release Linux path but a documented floor elsewhere: the `linux` job sets `GOTOOLCHAIN: 'go1.27.1'` with `actions/setup-go@v5 go-version: '1.27.1'`, while `src/golib/go.mod` carries `toolchain go1.27.1` as the repo-visible floor — the `bottle` job builds through the split Homebrew formulae whose `depends_on 'go'` is unversioned, so under `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` an ambient newer Go is used as-is. JDK 21 (`actions/setup-java`) and .NET 10.0.x (`actions/setup-dotnet`) are pinned in CI. The pin consumers are the paths that actually build: the CI `linux` job (`cargo build --release`, which drives `build.rs`) and `bottle` job (via the split formulae), plus those formulae themselves; `install.sh` is download-only — it fetches prebuilt release tarballs and never builds a frontend — so it consumes no toolchain and is not a pin consumer. Acceptance: `release.yml` names the exact Rust and Node pins and the Go release pin; the Rust pin and Node `engine-strict` hold on every path; the Go floor is documented for the bottle/ambient path.
